brief: The post-squeeze rally has moved prices but not resolved the underlying picture. SPX jumped from extreme oversold to major resistance near 7350-7400, where the 200-day average sits, with the longer-term trend near 7200. BTIG counts 42 NDX rallies of 6%+ below the 200-day average since 1985, with a median 30-day return of -5.35% and gains only 39% of the time; NDX futures stay below the 200-day and 21-day averages. S&P E-mini open interest rose $36.6bn as the index fell 5.9% into November 20 but fell only $7.9bn in Monday's squeeze, implying fresh longs or surviving shorts, or both. Jensen Huang's return has relieved AI names, but UBS expects self-funded AI spenders to diverge from debt-reliant ones. Bernstein finds data center exposure explains ~45% of AI valuation compression, hitting memory/server OEMs hardest while networking holds up. SNDK has derated to 2.5x forward earnings from a 10.4x three-year average. Asian hedge funds have de-grossed, cutting positioning risk; GS likes Nikkei-outperformance call spreads back toward October levels. Gold sits unusually far below its 200-day average, while Tether's 146.5 tonnes of gold (SocGen: ~65% new money) widen the buyer base. DXY's biggest down candle nears its mid-2023 downtrend line, pointing to a possible pause.
